newsitem.title: BOSNIA: British commander leaves Bosnia for Germany.
newsitem.headline: British commander leaves Bosnia for Germany.

text.p: Britain's Lieutenant-General Sir Michael Walker handed over command of international ground forces in Bosnia on Wednesday, transferring authority to U.S. General William Crouch in a brief ceremony in Sarajevo.
"We depart in the knowledge that we hand over a military ground force which is in good order and is highly professional," Walker told Crouch in remarks at the ceremony.
"We depart in the knowledge that we hand over former warring armies which are not in the same good professional order but which are at least securely tucked away in their barracks."
Walker returns to his post as commander of NATO's ACE Rapid Reaction Corps in Germany.

Deployed under the terms of the Dayton peace agreement in December of 1995, he brought more than 50,000 ground troops from 36 countries into Bosnia and achieved most of the tasks laid out in the accord's military section in three months.
Crouch, a four-star general, will command all NATO-led forces in Bosnia from a single, integrated headquarters in a major reorganisation.

British Lieutenant-General Roddy Cordy-Simpson will serve as Deputy Commander, Operations, under Crouch. Under the old system Cordy-Simpson would have had his own headquarters and independent command of ground forces.
